name: Pirate Chain
rootCause: A transaction validation vulnerability in Pirate Chain source code allowed the unauthorized creation of approximately 39.8 million ARRR, increasing the total supply by about 20%. The newly minted funds were transferred into the Sapling shielded pool. NonKYC identified suspicious deposits, restricted the associated accounts, and blocked withdrawals. The exploit combined two validation failures: bypassing the issuance check and incorrect interpretation of the output scripts. dPoW operators suspended notarizations as a precaution, and exchanges/pools were asked to pause operations while a recovery plan is developed.

name: KolanHook
rootCause: KolanHook settles its escrowed ETH buy-windows at the same Uniswap v4 pool's instantaneous spot price with no TWAP or bound and accept() is ungated once a window has expired, so the attacker flash-borrows 6.7 WETH from Balancer, swaps it to move the KLN spot, then calls accept() on two expired windows it does not own so _closeWindow() mispositions their escrowed ETH as single-sided liquidity around the manipulated price and runs an unbounded buyback, and reverses the swap back through that freshly placed ETH liquidity before repaying the loan for a 1.279453 ETH net gain. Lost: 1.279453 ETH net to the attacker EOA on Ethereum (surplus 1.279914429958618589 ETH after the 6.7 WETH Balancer flash loan is repaid, minus ~0.00046 ETH gas), draining KolanHook's full 2.309861 ETH of escrowed window funds

name: UNCX Network V2
rootCause: VestingManager pools every deposit of a given token in one contract and release() pays a slice of the full contract balance over a global share count, release() debits that global count but leaves the position's deposited shares in place and cancel() then debits the same shares a second time, so the attacker flash-borrows each token, creates self-owned vestings whose tranches are already elapsed and so instantly releasable, releases and cancels soft helper vestings to shrink the share denominator while donating token straight into the pool to raise the balance, then releases a payout vesting against the corrupted denominator and inflated balance to over-withdraw the other vesters backing tokens across five ERC-20s. Lost: ~88-89K USD across five ERC-20s on Ethereum, retained after the per-token flash loans are repaid and each reproduced to the wei against the tx transfer logs (EDGEN 55,601,598.708417972560603048, ZC 9,055,847.637887682268154756, pepecoin 40,155.284285661160205717, LO0P 65,372.217059159993437512, PAAL 113,657.766933968), the working capital flash-borrowed per token from Uniswap V3 (EDGEN), Uniswap V2 (pepecoin, PAAL) and Uniswap V4 (ZC, LO0P) and repaid in the same leg

name: Gamdom
rootCause: Crypto gambling platform Gamdom was attacked on October 13, 2026, due to an unauthorized server connection, resulting in approximately $4.2 million stolen from hot wallets. The incident affected multiple blockchains; the platform went offline for investigation and moved remaining hot wallet funds to cold storage.

name: Papertrade
rootCause: Papertrade, a synthetic perpetuals platform with up to 1000x leverage built on Hyperliquid’s HyperEVM, suffered a ~$1.28 million loss about 8 hours after its Oct. 10, 2026 launch. A wallet moved ETH prices on Hyperliquid (via large buys/sells) while holding highly leveraged positions on Papertrade that settled against the manipulated BBO midpoint, extracting profits from the platform’s shared USDC liquidity pool. Papertrade attributed it to overly permissive open-interest limits at launch and tightened them.

name: Ethervista
rootCause: EtherVista’s liquidity pool was exploited due to an integer overflow in the K-invariant check inside EtherVistaPair.swap(). Both reserves are uint112, so their product can wrap around and the check can pass even when the real reserve product drops sharply. The attacker registered a self-controlled contract as an authorized router and ran two crafted swaps to drain WETH and VISTA, with a loss of about $18,600.

name: X7Finance
rootCause: X7Pioneer's claimRewards() adds the unaccounted ETH balance delta into totalRewards on every call but only refreshes lastETHBalance when claimable is non-zero, so calling it with an empty tokenIds array re-counts the same donated delta each time and inflates the per-token reward until a single owned NFT drains the whole pool, the ~26.96 ETH donation supplied by a flash loan and repaid from the drain. Lost: ~6.78 ETH to the attacker on Ethereum (attacker EOA balance rose 6.777538 ETH; this reconstruction nets 6.793749214542107991 ETH, the difference being the on-chain Aave flash-loan premium and gas, neither modeled); the single draining claimRewards([300]) pays 33.756919822234785023 ETH, matching the on-chain RewardsClaimed to the wei, with the ~26.96 ETH donation capital returned

name: BitBay
rootCause: the UsdcDaiV4Vault _withdraw liquidity==0 branch pays the vault entire DAI and USDC balance to the caller with no share-weighted cap, and reposition() is permissionless once the tick is outside the narrow LP range, so the attacker deposits one wei for a single share, swaps the Uniswap v4 pool to push the tick onto tickUpper, calls reposition to recompute a position whose liquidity rounds to zero and leaves the pooled funds as raw balance, then redeems that one share to sweep the whole 14838 DAI pool. Lost: 14838.466608989135865711 DAI swept from the vault by a single 1-wei share on Polygon (reproduced to the wei against the on-chain Withdrawn amount), the attacker then unwound the drained DAI plus flash-loaned capital to a net ~14,813 USDC profit

name: 79th Vault
rootCause: An operator hot-wallet private key of 79th Vault was compromised. Using an OPERATOR_ROLE function, the attacker moved 2.01 million 79AU out of the PancakeSwap 79AU/USDT pair in seven transfers, sold them back in about 95 swaps, cut the pool’s USDT reserves from about $15,200,000 to about $3,900,000, and cashed out 16,249 BNB (about $12,500,000). Forty-one seconds later the same operator key sent 3.79 BNB to the attacker address.

name: MakerDAO ETH-A Liquidation Keeper Bot
rootCause: A Tornado Cash-funded address called an unprotected drain function on a dormant MakerDAO ETH-A liquidation keeper. The upgradeable proxy had won auctions #1457–1460 in 2020 (200 WETH total) but never called deal(), leaving the collateral in the Flipper. The attacker called deal(), moved the collateral to the keeper via Vat.flux, then used GemJoin.exit() to withdraw 200 WETH to an attacker-chosen address and unwrap it to ETH. The flaw was in the third-party keeper, not MakerDAO core.

name: Set Protocol
rootCause: a second RebalancingSetTokenV3 vault (ETHMACOAPY) hit by the same permissionless actualizeFee() divCeil rounding, the attacker issues the rebalancing set then donates the residual base set into the vault own backing so the zero-fee recompute bumps unitShares from 12253 to 12264, then redeems the same quantity for more collateral than was deposited, the ~116,000 WETH issue/redeem size supplied fee-free by an Aave-v3-fork flash loan. Lost: 4.047988247781965824 WETH to the attacker in the first tx (reproduced to the wei) on Ethereum; two independent EOAs drained the ETHMACOAPY rebalancing set across two txs two blocks apart for ~8.11 WETH total, this PoC reconstructs the first tx (0xb54c77dae4c5ff8664779bacfb56d75242f39005b0b7778109d2f9033b9e8fc2) only, the ~116,000 WETH working capital borrowed and repaid in the same tx via a zero-premium Aave-v3-fork flash loan

name: MakerDAOFlipKeeper
rootCause: the dormant ETH-A flip-keeper proxy's drain selector has no ds-auth check, so anyone can call it to make the keeper vat.hope() a caller-supplied worker and then deal its four undealt 2020 ETH-A auctions and flux/exit the freed 200 WETH of collateral out. Lost: exactly 200 ETH (200.000000000000000000 WETH, 0xad78ebc5ac6200000 wei, reproduced with zero variance) to a fresh attacker on Ethereum; the dormant keeper proxy's unprotected drain settled its four undealt 2020 ETH-A liquidation auctions (#1457-1460, 50 WETH each) and swept the freed collateral out - not a MakerDAO core bug, the keeper impl's drain selector simply omits the ds-auth modifier that the contract's other functions carry

name: Based Visa Card Internal Dashboard
rootCause: Web3 financial platform Based discovered that an unauthorized third party had accessed an internal dashboard used to manage the Based Visa Card program and contained the incident shortly after detection. KYC data collected by the card issuer for some cardholders (including name, ID/passport number, date of birth, and address) may have been obtained. Card numbers, CVV, PIN, ID photos, liveness records, the Based Wallet, and card funds were not affected, and cards continue to work normally. Affected users were notified by email, authorities were informed, and users were warned about phishing and social-engineering risks.

name: MALT
rootCause: the MALT/DAI sLP runs its below-peg price recovery inside swap() before sending the output, pulling DAI from the Capital Source treasury into the pool, then checks its constant-product invariant against the final balances without separating the injected treasury DAI from the caller's own input, so a negligible 1 DAI swap is credited with thousands of injected DAI and releases a disproportionate MALT output. Lost: 13,440.581562307921517594 DAI net profit to the attacker (exactly reproduced) on Polygon; the Capital Source treasury was drained of 12,744.644506590589136718 DAI across two below-peg rebalance injections, the attacker paying just 1 DAI per exploit swap and arbitraging the extracted MALT out on QuickSwap - the ~$72K figure in the original alert does not match the on-chain reconstruction

name: GoldPesa
rootCause: the GPX V4 hook rebalances protocol liquidity inside beforeSwap via a burn and TAKE_PAIR that run in the attacker's own open PoolManager unlock, and never checks the PositionManager deltas are settled first, so an unsettled mint debt parked in the same unlock nets against the hook's burn credit and the attacker walks the freed USDC out. Lost: 114,999.999186 USDC (exactly reproduced) on Base; the GPX/USDC V4 pool's protocol liquidity was burned by the hook's own hourly rebalance, and its 148,868.602188 USDC burn credit was split by the shared-unlock delta bug - 33,868.603002 USDC reached the hook while 114,999.999186 USDC paid off the attacker's unsettled mint debt and then exited to the attacker, funded by a 175,000 USDC Morpho flash loan repaid in the same tx

name: Microsoft’s official X account
rootCause: Microsoft’s official X account was accessed without authorization for about 30 minutes. Attackers changed the profile picture to Clippy, followed and reposted an impersonator account, and promoted an unauthorized Clippy meme coin to roughly 13 million followers; a later “apology” post was also unauthorized and deleted. Microsoft told The Verge and others that the account was secured, the posts removed, and that it never authorized any token tied to Clippy or $MSFT.

name: NEAR Intents
rootCause: A wallet funded with 10 USDT drained $3.87M from a BNB Chain vault serving NEAR Intents using valid signed authorizations. After a 48-hour ultimatum, the team announced a full recovery and closed its investigation; the full story of the failure remains unclear.

name: FlashLoopAdapter
rootCause: a Safe module authenticates its caller by asking that caller whether the module is enabled (self-attestation) and then makes an unconstrained call to a caller-supplied router, letting a fake Safe drive the adapter into draining real Safes that enabled it. Lost: 114.096151 WETH (~$305k, exactly reproduced) on Ethereum; two Safes that enabled the module as a victim were emptied - Safe #1 lost 1306.48 weETH of Aave collateral once its 1335.26 WETH debt was repaid, Safe #2 lost 6.426 weETH, all swapped to WETH via ODOS for the attacker's net

name: SKYDAO
rootCause: sell-path controller burns the pair's SKYDAO and syncs before the net sell is credited, latching a near-zero reserve that a direct pair.swap drains for the pair's entire USDT. Lost: 59,914.12 USDT net to the attacker (exactly reproduced) on BNB Chain; the SKYDAO/USDT PancakeSwap V2 pair lost its entire 183,482.88 USDT reserve, drained by a direct pair.swap against the reserve the sell-path burn+sync latched to ~0

name: MCN Labs
rootCause: The MCN Labs–related LPBonus contract used inconsistent MSN reserve values in reward accounting. Accrual updated the reward index with the reserve at that moment, while withdrawal applied a user weight based on the reserve at claim time. The attacker first lowered the reserve to ~89.33 MSN during accrual, then raised it to ~491.11 MSN before calling UserRemoveLp, allowing a newly registered LP to claim ~1,442,165.71 FIST against only ~940,041.61 FIST of intervening reward funding—about $92,600 in losses.

name: MUS
rootCause: deposit refunds a first-deposit bonus and also credits it as withdrawable allocation, so a single deposit-withdraw from a fresh address returns more ETH than deposited. Lost: ~0.400168 ETH per deposit-withdraw cycle (exactly reproduced) on Ethereum; the MUS pool's standing 5.335 ETH was drained to 0 across the attack block, reported campaign total ~$36.9k across many fresh addresses

name: MUSystem
rootCause: MUSystem’s deposit() counted the first-deposit bonus in both the immediate ETH refund and the user’s MUS allocation, while withdraw() allowed same-transaction redemption without capping returned ETH to the amount deposited. Sixteen fresh addresses repeated this cycle and drained ETH from the contract, causing about $36,900 in losses.

name: PositionManager
rootCause: deposit values the vault's existing USDT at the manipulable PancakeSwap V3 spot price, so crashing the spot before depositing mints inflated shares that withdraw redeems in the same transaction. Lost: 32,080.604282 USDT (exactly reproduced) on BNB Chain; one atomic tx crashed the USDT/BTCB spot with an 8,000,000 USDT swap, then ran 24 deposit(1,000,000 USDT)/withdraw cycles to drain the vault's own PancakeSwap V3 position, the pool losing 32,096.098596 USDT

name: LPBonus
rootCause: reserve inconsistency between reward accrual and LP withdrawal lets a manipulated MSN reserve inflate an LP reward claim. Lost: ~92,607 USDT (~$92.6k) on BNB Chain; one LP position claimed 1,442,165.713011 FIST against an accrual that funded ~940,041.612768 FIST, extracted by flash-swapping the MSN reserve down at accrual and back up at withdrawal

name: Fake GIWA Bridge
rootCause: Scammers deployed a fake GIWA L2 network using the legitimate Chain ID 9134, complete with a functional bridge and batcher. Approximately 1,335 addresses bridged ~767.65 ETH believing it was the official mainnet launch. The attackers drained ~766.25 ETH (~$2M). The real GIWA mainnet had not launched. DYORSWAP initially listed the fake network due to the matching Chain ID and later compensated affected users from its treasury.

name: DAOstack
rootCause: permissionless newOrganization lets an attacker hijack an existing Reputation contract and drain the Avatar. Lost: 4.025 ETH (full Genesis Alpha treasury); attacker minted 20,000 REP against the victim's real Reputation contract (supply 9,738.6 to 29,738.6, ~67% majority after a 200 REP GenesisProtocol vote-cost burn) and used it to self-install as a full-permission scheme

name: Bitget
rootCause: An attacker drained $387.5 million from Bitget’s hot and warm wallets after breaching third-party security products and reaching its wallet system. No keys stolen, Bitget says; freezes barely dented the loss, and the products remain unnamed. Who audits the guards?

name: Duelbits
rootCause: An attacker moved ~$6.07 million from Duelbits' hot wallets across five chains in a suspected private-key compromise, including the replacement wallet named after its $4.6 million theft in 2024. It reopened days later, cause still undisclosed. What changed since 2024?

name: Payy Network
rootCause: Payy’s Ethereum bridge contract was exploited and fully drained, with about 1,832,149 USDC leaving the contract. Payy said the stolen funds were users’ non-custodial deposits to Payy Network / Payy Wallet, paused all transactions, and said it is working on fund retrieval and a root-cause analysis.

name: Limit Break Payment Processor
rootCause: An attacker exploited a bug in Limit Break’s Payment Processor V2, abusing stale Magic Eden EVM marketplace approvals to steal blue-chip NFTs via zero-price “sales” and to drain WETH in reverse. V2 could not be paused, so Yuga Labs VP of Blockchain @0xQuit led a whitehat rescue that moved 23,155 NFTs worth over $5.7M to safety; about 660 WETH could not be recovered in time. Magic Eden and Limit Break later urged users to revoke V2/V3 approvals immediately.

name: Meter
rootCause: Blockaid reported an ongoing exploit of Meter.io’s Meter Passport bridge on BNB Chain. An attacker minted a large amount of unbacked wrapped MTRG through the bridge and sold part of it on PancakeSwap. About $2,300,000 of unbacked wMTRG had been minted in roughly two transactions when the alert went out, and the attack was still ongoing.

name: PancakeV3SwapHelper
rootCause: Signed Swap Delta Accounting Error. Lost: ~1.6488688845 BNB (~$1.3K)

name: The personal X account of Nano Labs founder Jack Kong
rootCause: The personal X account of Nano Labs founder Jack Kong was compromised. Attackers used it to promote a fake AI trading token called Binance World Assets ($BWA), claiming it would use trading fees on BNB Chain to trade bStocks and share profits with holders. Nano Labs’ official account later stated that the posts were unauthorized, that the company had not issued or endorsed any such token, and warned users not to click links or send funds to any contracts.

name: Astroport
rootCause: Astroport (a Cosmos ecosystem DEX) announced a security incident on the Neutron chain that may have resulted in the theft of admin privileges for its contracts. Neutron has halted chain operations for investigation, and the project advised users to immediately withdraw liquidity from all Astroport pools across chains. Terra-side contracts were unaffected.

name: Drop
rootCause: The Drop project suffered an attack via a malicious governance proposal, through which the attacker transferred treasury funds, resulting in a loss of approximately $4.4 million.

name: RWC Token
rootCause: The RWC token on BNB Smart Chain was exploited with a flash loan. An unprotected burn function let the attacker destroy RWC sitting in the PancakeSwap RWC/USDT pair and call sync() to rewrite reserves, inflating the price before selling back. The pool lost about 109,460.85 USDT in one transaction. The attacker kept about 39,964.07 USDT; the remaining about 69,496.78 USDT was routed to the project’s company and platform wallets by the token’s fee logic.

name: TheRedVillage
rootCause: ungated PolygonTRVRouter forwardRequest relays an attacker-supplied upgradeTo through the router's _authorizeUpgrade role on the SeasonService UUPS proxy, installing a malicious implementation that uses the proxy's TRVZooKeeper roles to pull every player's approved WETH and sweep the vault. Lost: 31.426018474517367982 WETH (~$80.7K) swept from TRVZooKeeper on Polygon; 299 players with standing WETH approvals were pulled for 31.350379502001368 WETH and the vault's pre-existing 0.075638972516 WETH was swept with them, reproduced to the wei

name: DoinGud
rootCause: acceptOffer replay via missing offer cleanup on the amount=0 path. Lost: 35,380.154566 USDC net (two byte-identical acceptOffer calls each paid out 35,486.935717 USDC from escrow; funded via a UniV2 flash swap, repaid 35,593.716868 USDC)

name: GaslessReservoirEnabler
rootCause: erc20WithTransfersAndExecute lets a whitelisted module run unvalidated transferFrom calldata. Lost: 8.72 WETH (~$23.8K) across 466 victims with standing approvals to the Enabler; PoC reproduces 3 victims, 2.3546 WETH (~$6.4K, ~27% of the WETH-leg loss)

name: The Internet Token
rootCause: permissionless swapV3 with caller-supplied pool lets a fake callback mint INT arbitrarily. Lost: 764,145,702 INT + 5.846988 WETH (attacker minted 925.41M INT total, dumped 161.27M into the real INT/WETH pool for the WETH, reproduced to the wei)

name: SingularityNET
rootCause: An attacker accessed SingularityNET’s cloud infrastructure. Valid bridge signatures authorized AGIX, WMTX and CGV mints; NTX was minted directly, and 8.72 million FET was drained, and $2.29M in gross liquid proceeds traced. When a signature is treated as proof, who checks whether it tells the truth?

name: Fetch.ai
rootCause: An attacker used a leaked conversion-authorizer / bridge backend signing key to call conversionIn() on Fetch.ai’s Ethereum token-conversion contract and drain about 8,721,530 FET (~$1.53 million). The same wallet cluster then minted about 408.5 million unauthorized NTX via a NuNet deployer key and later expanded the attack to related ASI Alliance bridge/converter infrastructure.

name: NuNet
rootCause: An attacker gained control of NuNet’s Ethereum deployer/minting private key and called mint() on the NTX token contract, issuing 408,532,878.13 NTX to the attacker’s address. The mint function had no supply-cap check, so possession of the key was enough to create new tokens. PeckShield valued the unauthorized mint at approximately $462,730 at the time of the incident.

name: MultiversX
rootCause: An attacker attempted to exploit a virtual-machine-level atomicity issue on the MultiversX mainnet, causing invalid on-chain state changes. The network was paused to contain further impact. Engineers prepared a fix for validation on a shadow fork and are evaluating a targeted recovery that would keep finalized history and legitimate user state while reversing only incident-related invalid changes. Users were told not to submit or rebroadcast transactions and not to deposit or withdraw EGLD or ESDT via exchanges or bridges.

name: Blink Wallet
rootCause: A software flaw at Blink Wallet allowed an attacker to access and empty a few dozen custodial accounts. Services were paused. Non-custodial wallets and the large majority of funds were unaffected. The vulnerability was patched the same day. On September 24, Blink said every affected account had been restored to its exact pre-incident balance. The attacker also accessed account information of about 3,400 other users, but no funds, names, IDs or addresses were taken from those accounts.

name: Likwid
rootCause: missing pairDelta update in leverage=0 margin borrow freezes AMM quote. Lost: 74.31 BNB (reproduced to within 3 wei)

name: Nostra Money Market
rootCause: A rigged pool fed Nostra's oracle a fake NSTR price, 8,306x real value, unlocking a $3.5 million borrow on Starknet. Pragma says it warned Nostra the feed was high-risk beforehand. Money market is still paused, and still no post-mortem.

name: Flamincome
rootCause: permissionless Convex stakeFor inflates Strategy NAV and lets VaultYUSDT overpay on withdrawAll. Lost: ~$345.9K USDT net attacker profit (gross Strategy loss ~$595K in aUSDT+USDT)

name: Nimiq
rootCause: GSN forwarder skips signature check, relying solely on attacker-chosen paymaster. Lost: ~$50,463.79 (USDC, USDT0, USDC.e drained from a swap-liquidity wallet's standing approvals)

name: PrimeFinance
rootCause: permissionless stale signed oracle report overwrite drains lending pool. Lost: ~425.5 WHYPE (~$33.4K) drained from the lending pool reserve

name: Startale
rootCause: transient storage init flag outlives the constructor and lets anyone reinitialize an ERC7579 account and drain it. Lost: 427.551160 USDC drained in this batch tx (32.555561 USDC reproduced across 3 of 23 victim accounts; ~$2,876 USDC+USDT aggregate across 41 known batches)

name: RsETHSafeModule
rootCause: nested self-referential multicall authorization bypass drains Gnosis Safe via DELEGATECALL. Lost: 2,900 aEthrsETH (~$7.8M gross; 2,882.37 rsETH / ~$7.73M net to the MEV frontrunner)

name: Unknown Gnosis Safe Wallet
rootCause: An unidentified user’s Gnosis Safe wallet on Ethereum was drained of about $7,730,000. The attacker exploited an authorization bypass in a Router multicall function, used the victim Safe module to DelegateCall attacker-crafted data, injected aEthrsETH into a malicious Uniswap V4 hooked pool, then swapped and redeemed it as rsETH. Kelp later placed a 24-hour pause on an address that received the stolen rsETH.

name: DCENT Wallet
rootCause: On September 16, 2026, DCENT (formerly D'CENT) issued an urgent security alert stating that abnormal asset transfers had been detected in its mobile App Wallet (software wallet) and that an emergency investigation was underway. Initial findings indicate the issue is limited to the App Wallet, with no confirmed impact on hardware wallets themselves. Users holding assets in the App Wallet, or using the same mnemonic for both the App Wallet and a hardware wallet, are strongly advised to immediately transfer funds to a secure hardware wallet or other trusted address, and to remain vigilant against scams.

name: Bonfire
rootCause: missing caller authorization lets anyone force-sell any approved holder's tokens. Lost: ~66 BNB (~$47-50K); 58.78 BNB reproduced from a 5-victim subset (~98.7% of tokens drained)

name: Long Bridge
rootCause: Long’s custodial bridge released 46.7928 WETH (about $118,000) from its Robinhood Chain vault after a third-party RPC fed the keeper fabricated Arc withdrawal events. No on-chain contract or key was breached. The team halted the keeper, rebuilt verification, and refilled the vault the same day from platform revenue. Users did not lose funds.

name: Chainflip AMM
rootCause: Cross-chain protocol Chainflip was exploited on its TRON USDT integration. The attacker abused TRON memo handling by attaching a custom memo to a transaction already signed by validators, causing the system to treat the same deposit as a separate failed swap and issue a duplicate refund. The attack was repeated eight times over about 90 minutes, producing six unauthorized payouts totaling 736,442.17 USDT. A pending user swap of 115,654.41 USDT remains safely in the vault. The network is paused, a fix is ready, restart is expected as early as Monday, and affected users will be made whole.

name: YamFinance
rootCause: dormant-DAO quorum governance takeover drains legacy UMA farming contracts. Lost: ~$121K (48.085 WETH + 763.101 UMA)

name: SpiralHookV2
rootCause: Uniswap V4 spot-price borrow plus tx.origin-keyed same-block guard bypass. Lost: ~10.70728 ETH (reproduced exact to the wei)

name: ether.fi Liquid
rootCause: Users of ether.fi Liquid (liquidETH) lost ~15.45 ETH after an attacker exploited missing access control in AtomicQueue.solve() on the caller-supplied solver parameter. The attacker crafted a malicious AtomicRequest, forced already-approved victim addresses to act as solver, and drained funds via existing ERC-20 allowances with transferFrom. About 11 users were affected.

name: ORB
rootCause: leveraged pool buyout + refund-before-sell reentrancy drains burnLP-depleted reserve. Lost: ~44.9-45 BNB (~$32,610.72)

name: GDC
rootCause: chained EOA bypass, liquidity misclassification, burn mismatch, and reentrant tax-free exit. Lost: ~35.34 BNB (35.337151495976986490 BNB reproduced exact to the wei)

name: Symbiosis
rootCause: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Symbiosis’ Bitcoin Bridge (BridgeV2) by abusing incorrect parsing of Bitcoin transaction data and negative fee settings, minting approximately 2622^{62}2^{62} unbacked syBTC (notional face value ~46.1 billion) across BSC, Ethereum and Rootstock within about four minutes, then sold ~4.39 WBTC on Ethereum’s Uniswap V4 for ~$336,000. The team immediately paused native BTC routes, isolated the affected component, evacuated ~15.2 BTC of portal funds to reserve addresses, and offered a 20% white-hat bounty. The post-mortem confirmed total losses for LPs and affected users at 9.97 BTC. Other routes (EVM, TRON, TON, etc.) remained unaffected.

name: Dominion
rootCause: Dominion Market’s Solana silver token $SILV suffered a treasury multisig compromise. With 3-of-5 keys, the attacker emptied the treasury and pulled SILV from loans, dumping about 46,909 tokens (face value ~$3 million) into thin DEX pools and realizing about $238,000 as the peg broke. The team pulled liquidity, rotated hardware, froze tokens bought in the incident window, and planned USDC refunds plus a repeg.

name: Nomic
rootCause: An attacker exploited a bug in Nomic’s custom forwarding mechanism to double-spend nBTC and send unbacked vouchers to Osmosis. Osmosis and IBC themselves were not compromised. 39.84 nBTC of the minted supply sat in Alloyed BTC (~36% of its backing). Osmosis froze Nomic and Alloyed BTC flows, upgraded with validators, and froze 22.65 BTC in the attacker’s address. Governance will be asked to seize those funds and cover the rest from the community pool.

name: Zentra Finance
rootCause: aToken burn safeguard clamps to zero, repayWithATokens clears debt without burning. Lost: ~140,000 ctUSD + 30 USDC.e (~$143K)

name: Amnext
rootCause: The old BNB Chain DeFi protocol Amnext (AMC), a no-loss lottery/prize-pool product, was exploited. The attacker mass-minted Ticket AMC and drained about 154.02 WBNB from the protocol via PancakeSwap, causing a loss of approximately $ 116,100.

name: BeatXswap
rootCause: slot0 spot-price oracle with no TWAP guard drains vesting BTX reserves. Lost: ~$63.7K USDT net profit (2,984,557 BTX / ~$77.5K drained from two vesting reserves)

name: OMNI404
rootCause: ERC-404 dual ID/amount transfer interpretation drains pool WETH. Lost: 2.427 WETH (run() leg reproduced here; ~3.02 ETH across the full 4-tx block)

name: EtherFiAtomicQueue
technique: missing solver access control drains victim allowances
rootCause: missing solver access control drains victim allowances. Lost: ~15.45 ETH (9 real victims' standing liquidETH allowances drained)

name: UnifiProtocol
rootCause: unregistered caller-supplied pool trusted for reward eligibility and math. Lost: ~5.86 BNB (treasury still holds ~9.17 BNB, contract unpaused — bug remains re-exploitable)

name: EnsoFinance
rootCause: short-window Uniswap V3 TWAP oracle enables ~9x overvalued strategy deposit. Lost: ~5.6 ETH (5.277 ETH realized in this PoC after slippage selling looted UNI/AAVE/MKR back to WETH)

name: WealthManagementV2
rootCause: The WealthManagementV2 contract lost funds after owner privileges were suspected of being illegally transferred (possibly due to a leaked private key). The attacker-controlled owner instantly set extreme plan parameters (period=0, interestMultiplier/unlockMultiplier=528,300,000) via updatePlanConfig with no timelock or bounds, minted inflated interest by investing and redeeming in the same transaction, then unlocked and withdrew the funds via a second investment, resulting in a loss of 26,414 USDT.

name: OrderFactory
rootCause: missing access control on createOrderForBuyer drains buyer accounts. Lost: ~20.247 ETH this tx (5 buyers drained; reported incident total ~24.7 ETH)

name: Cozy V2
rootCause: unverified UMA Optimistic Oracle trigger enables unbacked protection-token redemption. Lost: ~160,776 USDC.e (~$160K)

name: Unnamed BSC DEX Router
rootCause: An unnamed DEX router on BNB Chain was exploited because uniswapV3SwapCallback did not authenticate a real V3 pool. The attacker used a fake pool, set victims as payer, and drained existing token allowances via transferFrom, stealing about 62.28 WBNB from 29 wallets in one transaction.

name: RouterDrain
rootCause: permissionless swap entry lets a fake V3 pool abuse router allowances. Lost: ~62.28 WBNB across 29 victims (3 reconstructed here: OCEAN, Kandura, SATURN)

name: Liquid Network
rootCause: An actor exploited a range-proof cache-key collision in Elements to mint ~4,000 unbacked L-BTC, draining $320 million from Liquid Network. The actor returned 3,400 BTC and kept roughly 598.5 BTC. Was it a bounty or theft? The dispute continues.

name: Rocket Perp
rootCause: An attacker exploited a dormant, illiquid perpetual market on Rocket. Using a burner account, they posted orders at artificially inflated prices and traded against themselves to generate fake profits on one account while bankrupting the burner. The profitable account then withdrew approximately $287K in positive PnL from the Bridge, with the loss socialized across the platform. Deposits, withdrawals and trading were paused.

name: Secured Finance Lending
rootCause: same-block self-trade manipulates getMarketUnitPrice to fabricate collateral. Lost: ~0.9 WBTC (~$72K single-drain; ~$104K across all actors exploiting the same public bug)

name: Dream Health Chain
rootCause: Dream Health Chain’s staking/reward contracts on BSC were exploited for about 71,851 USDT. A broken award state machine allowed a claimed reward to be reset with a tiny or zero-effective DHC deposit, so the same fixed payout could be claimed repeatedly from the shared pool. The attacker looped pledge and claim, then sold about 542,070 DHC into the DHC-USDT pool.

name: DHC
technique: repeatable claim due to missing claimed-flag
rootCause: repeatable claim due to missing claimed-flag. Lost: ~$71.8K USDT

name: Reddio RedSonic
rootCause: cross-share-class balance double-count via permissionless registerErc20. Lost: ~9.25 ETH

name: Notional V2
rootCause: ERC1155 fCash mint overflow drains escrow. Lost: ~69,257.37 DAI + ~1,658,524.86 USDC (~$1.73M)

name: XRPH Wallet
rootCause: On the evening of September 3, 2026, approximately 4,011 XRPH Wallet user accounts suffered unauthorized transactions involving XRPH, XRPHAI and other assets, with roughly $452,000 stolen. Funds were collected, bridged via NEAR Intents to Ethereum, and converted to about 445,198 DAI, which remains unmoved in one address. The project confirmed no issue with the XRP Ledger itself, took the app offline, and is investigating.

name: GebProxyActions
rootCause: The GebProxyActions contract was exploited due to missing caller access control in the quitSystem function. Victims had previously called it directly instead of via DSProxy delegatecall, setting ownsSAFE[safe] to the GebProxyActions contract. The attacker called GebProxyActions.quitSystem(manager, safe, dst) directly, bypassing GebSafeManager’s safeAllowed check and transferring collateral to themselves.

name: ReflexerGEB
technique: Shared GebProxyActions library registered as SAFE owner
rootCause: Shared GebProxyActions library registered as SAFE owner. Lost: ~5.9436 ETH (~$14K, drained from 4 SAFEs in one tx: IDs 3, 5, 8, 18)

name: Aquifer
rootCause: Solana-based proprietary AMM Aquifer was exploited for about $2.5 million. Public reporting points to compromised protocol-linked wallets or admin credentials rather than a confirmed smart-contract bug. The attacker operated addresses on both Solana and Ethereum. The same day, Aquifer’s Solana upgrade authority posted an on-chain white-hat offer: return at least 80% of stolen assets by September 3, 2026, 14:00 UTC to designated recovery addresses, and keep up to 20% as a bounty, in exchange for no civil claims by the project.

name: Ankr
rootCause: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Ankr’s ankrFLOW liquid staking contract to mint approximately 8.6 million unbacked ankrFLOW tokens, then used them as collateral with More Markets’ E-mode to drain about 15.5 million WFLOW (~$410,000 at spot) from the lending reserve. The attacker realized roughly $246,000 after slippage. The Flow Foundation stated the root cause was in Ankr’s Solidity contract, not Flow EVM or More Markets.

name: Float Protocol
rootCause: Uniswap V3 spot price manipulation of Hypervisor LP shares. Lost: ~$28,000 (10.71 ETH)

name: Tectonic
rootCause: An attacker pumped Tectonic's TONIC token roughly 300x and borrowed $120.4 million against the inflated collateral. Cronos rolled back 10,961 blocks to recover $111.2 million; $9.19 million had already left the chain and remains unrecovered.

name: Balancer V1
rootCause: joinswapPoolAmountOut rounding drain across 5 pools. Lost: ~$110,839 for this DPI/USDC/WETH/WBTC pool (~$234K aggregate across all 5 vulnerable pools)

name: Full Sail
rootCause: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Switchboard’s production code to add a controlled key to a live oracle, published false prices roughly 100 times below market, deposited into Full Sail vaults at distorted values, then restored prices and withdrew more than deposited.

name: Permapod
rootCause: Permapod experienced a security incident on ZIGChain on 29 August 2026. The incident's cause, mechanism, and impact remain unknown, with no confirmed loss or root-cause details available. The root cause of the Permapod incident remains unknown due to the absence of technical, transaction, or post-mortem details in all available sources.

name: Fogo Foundation
rootCause: The Fogo Foundation experienced a compromise by an unknown actor, resulting in 400 million FOGO tokens being sent to a bad actor. The Foundation immediately alerted exchanges, law enforcement, and forensic experts. Initially stated no impact on the blockchain, but later halted the mainnet as a precaution to restrict associated addresses and prevent further asset movement. Mainnet was later restarted after recovering and permanently removing 237 million tokens.

name: Virtue
rootCause: On August 28, 2026, Virtue protocol on IOTA suffered a critical oracle signing key compromise, enabling an attacker to manipulate price feeds and mint roughly 4.94 million VUSD against a single IOTA deposit. The manipulated price soon triggered 47 liquidations across 45 user positions, freezing the protocol and causing up to $905,000 in affected collateral, with Virtue estimating damage at $455,000 and DefiLlama listing $894,500. Compromise of Switchboard oracle signing keys allowed attacker-controlled price reporting, bypassing Virtue's feed authentication and enabling artificial collateral valuation with no economic sanity or deviation checks.

name: Ajna V2
rootCause: liquidation accounting manipulation via self-controlled auction. Lost: ~$124.8K for this cbETH pool (1 of 7 pools hit by the same bug the same day, ~$775K aggregate)

name: Avici
rootCause: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in an outdated version of Rain’s Solana card contract used by Avici (and a few other programs). By submitting crafted signature bundles to gain unauthorized admin rights via AddCollateralAdmin and then withdrawing collateral, they drained $500,859.22 from 1,685 users’ card balances. Self-custodial wallets were unaffected. The contract was upgraded across all programs, and full refunds were promised.

name: Moonwell Lending
rootCause: Base-based DeFi lending protocol Moonwell was attacked. The attacker inflated the price of the low-liquidity token MAMO, posted it as collateral, and borrowed real assets such as cbBTC and USDC from markets including mCBTC and mUSDC.

name: CashCowCoin
technique: privileged burn + premature sync() drains PancakeSwap pair
rootCause: privileged burn + premature sync() drains PancakeSwap pair. Lost: ~165.47 WBNB (~$117.4K)

name: Steakhouse Financial
rootCause: Steakhouse Financial’s 2026-08-25 incident was reported as a $920,000 Ethereum loss tied to risk parameter abuse, but the accessible record does not identify the exact contract path, transaction hash, or recovered funds. Risk parameter abuse is the reported failure mode, but the exact parameter, contract, and state transition are not identified in the accessible sources.

name: CometDEX
rootCause: The BLND-USDC liquidity pool of CometDEX (Comet AMM) on the Stellar network was exploited due to an accounting bug that allowed same-asset swaps (USDC→USDC), corrupting reserve calculations. The attacker used flash loans from a Blend pool and repeated the process about 36 times to extract excess funds, resulting in a loss of approximately $717,518.92 USDC. Funds were subsequently moved.

name: Enjin
rootCause: unprotected registry reinitialization, manager takeover. Lost: 5,231,353 ENJ (~$142K)

name: FH Token
rootCause: sell-tax reserve mismatch via premature sync(). Lost: 19,999.018106552928530404 USDT (~$20K)

name: Nesa
rootCause: An attacker bridged 257.7 million NES, roughly $50 million, from Nesa to Ethereum in an incident consistent with the Cosmos EVM bug chain that hit MANTRA, TAC, and KiiChain. Nesa never published the mechanism; Bubblemaps estimated slippage cut net profit to roughly $60k.

name: TermFinance Vaults
rootCause: Governance capture via thinly-wrapped Aragon voting power. Lost: 2,841.743535791961701401 WETH (attacker net gain, ETH meta-vault)

name: warp.green
rootCause: The ERC-20 bridge of warp.green (a cross-chain messaging protocol between Chia and EVM chains) suffered an exploit due to a vulnerability in the Chia-side Chialisp puzzle. The attacker minted worthless CAT tokens, presented them as burned wUSDC, obtained validator signatures, and drained ~$93,000 USDC from the Base and Ethereum bridge contracts, later converting the funds to ETH. The CAT bridge (securing assets like wXCH) appears unaffected.

name: Arrakis V1
rootCause: Uniswap V3 spot-price manipulation of vault mint/burn. Lost: ~2.9414 ETH net attacker surplus (Arrakis V1 / G-UNI ENS-WETH vault)

name: KiiChain
rootCause: An attacker drained 148.3 million KII, worth roughly $9.7 million at the pre-exploit price, from KiiChain through the Cosmos EVM exploit class that also hit MANTRA and TAC. A halt immobilized 54.4% on-chain, but the rest had already crossed to BNB Chain.

name: TAC
rootCause: An attacker drained 2.985B TAC (~$7.5M) from its bonded-token pool via the Cosmos EVM underflow bug that hit MANTRA. TAC halted four hours too late, funds already bridged out. Cosmos Labs had the bug since April but apparently misjudged its severity.

name: The Sandbox
rootCause: LayerZero delegate hijack via approveAndCall. Lost: 10,000,000 SAND minted unbacked (~$517,170 face value, one of 400+ repeated txs in an ongoing campaign)

name: MANTRA Chain
rootCause: An attacker drained 720M MANTRA, worth $3.6 million per Mantra’s postmortem, through a confirmed Cosmos EVM underflow bug. The halt came too late for 94.7% of it, which had already reached an exchange. Three more chains fell to the same flaw days later.

name: BounceBit
rootCause: An attacker exploited a protocol-level authorization flaw in the Evmos stack, transferring approximately 286.5 million BB from nine mainnet accounts across 14 transactions without the owners’ authorization. No private keys were compromised, no signatures forged, and no wallets breached. BounceBit permanently sunset the L1 chain and reissued BB as a BEP-20 token on BNB Chain based on a pre-attack snapshot.

name: Allbridge
rootCause: Phantom deposit via unverified message attestation. Lost: ~189,751.554381 USDC

name: Maya Protocol
rootCause: Maya Protocol (MAYAChain) suffered a security vulnerability attack. The attacker exploited 6 chained edge-case bugs in Trade Account, outbound handling, and pool math, inflating accounting via false subsidy (e.g., ARB.LINK pool), then added/removed liquidity to extract ~48.87M CACAO and convert to ~20.83 BTC plus other assets, causing ~$1.7 million loss. The team paused global operations to fix the issues and seeks fund recovery.

name: Fox Market
rootCause: FoxMarket (a DeFi project on BSC) had its FoxLpBondsPool.stake() function calculate and fix _stakeAmount from a manipulable Pancake AMM spot quote before a large USDT→Fox swap. The attacker used flash loans to skew pair reserves, then addLiquidity used a mismatched ratio; Treasury.lpBonds() trusted the stale value, minted excess Fox tokens, and sent inviter rewards to an attacker-controlled address, which were sold in the same transaction.

name: Bodega Market
rootCause: Bodega Market's incident on 14 August 2026 remains classified by industry catalogues as oracle manipulation, with a reported loss of $3,600. No technical details, exploit transactions, or root-cause disclosure have been published. The mechanism and response are unknown. The incident is classified as 'oracle manipulation' in multiple catalogues, but the specific exploit mechanism, affected price feed, and contract vulnerability are undocumented.

name: Harmony Bridge
rootCause: Estimated $3.2 million lost after unauthenticated proof fields let old cross-shard receipts replay, crediting ONE without a source debit. Harmony confirmed an initial 4 billion ONE mint, its broader reconstruction reached 3.01 trillion. A rollback is planned and exchanges remain unnamed.

name: Coinsbuy
rootCause: $8.07 million  lost from Coinsbuy across TRON and Ethereum in under an hour, then refilled ten drained wallets within half a day. One blog post since, no follow-up, Twitter account dormant since 2020. Nobody has said what actually failed.

name: Coreum Bridge
rootCause: On August 9, 2026, the cross-chain bridge connecting the XRP Ledger and Coreum (now tx) was exploited. The attacker abused a flaw in the deposit-verification/relayer logic by creating fake deposits (self-transfers of the bridge’s own wrapped tokens with valid memos), tricking the relayers into authorizing real XRP withdrawals from the bridge’s reserve. Nearly 200,000 XRP (~$200,000) was drained in 94 multisig transactions over 97 minutes.

name: USM
rootCause: defund() price split-invariance rounding exploit. Lost: ~70.83 ETH

name: Oraichain
rootCause: Oraichain (AI Layer 1) suffered from a vulnerability in its EVM cross-chain transfer path, enabling unauthorized minting of ORAI tokens. The network has been halted since 04:00 UTC on August 9, 2026, with bridges, cross-chain routes, and public interfaces restricted. The exploit path has been identified and addressed; the team is working with partners and CEXs to limit fund movements and is preparing to burn the unauthorized minted balances and reconcile protocol states to restore the canonical ORAI supply.

name: Atomic Green
rootCause: Atomic Green (a non-custodial leveraged trading protocol on Arbitrum) was exploited due to a signature replay vulnerability. The same manager signature could be replayed across 21 different Uniswap V3 LP positions, combined with flashloan-based price manipulation, allowing the attacker to trigger unauthorized full LP burns and resulting in a loss of approximately 29,984.27 USDC.

name: Ravencoin
rootCause: Ravencoin suffered a consensus-level vulnerability in August 2026 that allowed attackers to forge invalid blocks by manipulating the block header, disrupting the network and prompting a coordinated chain recovery and emergency software patch. No direct user balance loss has been established, but the incident triggered a major chain reorganization and significant market impact. Ravencoin’s KAWPOW mining code did not validate that the nHeight field in a block header matched the block’s true position, allowing attackers to bypass the full proof of work and forge blocks. This broke the protocol’s core security assumption and led to multiple invalid blocks being appended to the main chain.

name: RRWallet
rootCause: Security firm Coinspect disclosed that RRWallet (RenrenBit’s wallet) generated vulnerable seed phrases due to a weak RNG in the CryptoJS library (Ill Bloom vulnerability, CVE-2026-71851), making private keys predictable and leading to theft. One user lost approximately $2 million.

name: LULA
rootCause: BNB Chain reserve manipulation attack resulting in approximately $578K loss. Detailed technical analysis available in BlockSec's weekly Web3 security roundup. Source: https://twitter.com/Phalcon_xyz/status/2085194687783313852

name: Panther Protocol
rootCause: Attacker submitted a governance proposal named 'zkp-reexploit' to upgrade each ZKP proxy to a drainer implementation. The attacker posted a 'yes' answer with 0.5 ETH bond. No honest party counter-bonded within the 12h timeout + 8h cooldown. The answer finalized and governance module executed the drain. Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2085673531409400047

name: Hyperliquid Malaysia
rootCause: On August 6, 2026, the Hyperliquid Malaysia community treasury suffered a private key compromise on Solana. No confirmed transaction or loss figure has been published. The incident affected a local group's wallet and not the Hyperliquid trading protocol itself. The incident was caused by the compromise of the private key controlling the Hyperliquid Malaysia community treasury wallet. The reviewed statements do not confirm exactly how the key was obtained or what method enabled the attacker to access the wallet.

name: KITE Foundation
rootCause: The KITE Foundation detected abnormal KITE token transfers on Ethereum mainnet, confirming that some wallet addresses had been compromised by hackers. The team urgently paused ERC-20 transfers and related cross-chain channels, with no asset losses to users or the project. A new contract was later deployed, airdropping new tokens 1:1 to legitimate addresses based on the snapshot at block 25,692,498, excluding attacker-controlled addresses.

name: StrongBlock
technique: governance takeover of an abandoned Governor
rootCause: governance takeover of an abandoned Governor. Lost: 32,695.761681 STRONG + 383,447.167299 STRNGR (~$72K)

name: Unistreets
rootCause: arbitrary call injection via unvalidated launch forwarding. Lost: ~17,743.91 USDC + ~0.0072 WETH (~$17.75K)

name: ZEUS
rootCause: ZEUS (Bitcoin Lightning Network wallet and LSP provider) infrastructure suffered a cybersecurity incident/attack within the last few hours; the attack was mitigated. Services were temporarily taken offline for a full systems audit out of caution; no customer funds were lost or at risk, and closed LSP channels will be replaced upon restoration. The incident appears limited to ZEUS infrastructure, with no evidence of a Lightning node software vulnerability.

name: Nereus
rootCause: NereusShapeshiftersMarket NFT marketplace (TransparentUpgradeableProxy 0x6de0...6d73) drained via malicious implementation upgrade. Proxy admin key (0x863b...4076, EIP-7702-delegated EOA) was compromised and used to call ProxyAdmin.upgradeAndCall, swapping implementation to a freshly deployed drainer contract (0x60f8...23d1). Drainer's selector 0x8961ec50 swept entire ETH balance to attacker address. Attacker (0xd9cb...8f5f) extracted 12.74 ETH. Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x125e0a7046004a5886cd0908907ae85bf8716567b4464e11570d588425b0bc93 Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2084871269854384356

name: RISEx
rootCause: On August 3, 2026, an unauthorized withdrawal of 673,011.56 USDC occurred from the RWA strategy linked to RISEx’s XLP vault due to a misconfiguration present since its July 13 deployment. The team detected it within minutes, patched it by 08:09 UTC, and fully compensated XLP depositors using a portion of July fees; the platform and other components continued operating normally.

name: AIC
technique: pair skim / reserve-mismatch exploit, flash-swap leveraged
rootCause: pair skim / reserve-mismatch exploit, flash-swap leveraged. Lost: ~32.36 BNB (~$21.5K)

name: MOKE
rootCause: settle() tx.origin check lets any EOA latch a manipulated MOKE/USDT price, then claim() mints inflated MOKE against it. Lost: ~1546.54 BNB (~41.68M MOKE over-minted)

name: LOOPSDAO
rootCause: LOOPSDAO’s LpdFi protocol on BSC was exploited. The attacker used a flash loan to manipulate the spot price of the thin PancakeSwap LPD/USDC pair (no TWAP or deviation guard), opened a massively inflated interest-bearing position with minimal LPD, and claimed interest right across the daily settlement boundary. This triggered the protocol to burn its own Cake-LP and pay out the inflated amount, draining approximately $690,000.

name: LpdFi
rootCause: Oracle vulnerability: LpdFi's price() function relied directly on PancakeSwap LPD/USDC pair spot reserves without TWAP protection. Attacker flash-borrowed USDC, manipulated reserves via donate+sync, inflated interest calculations, then claimed interest via removeLp() to drain the protocol's ~1.68M LP position. ~693.5K USDC extracted in single transaction. Attack Tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0x70bbe0aa3c7ef149ecb6128a06025885deaa8fef3f393a505d447d28ab3315d6 Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2084157533204197380

name: COLDCARD
rootCause: A firmware vulnerability silently routed Coldcard's hardware RNG for a guessable software fallback, letting attackers brute-force seeds offline. No phishing, no malware. $130 million reported stolen so far, at least 15 attackers, most funds still untouched, nobody caught.

name: Swan Treasury
rootCause: Off-chain signer key (0xdEb4...8284) hardcoded in ZhaiquanBuy contract was compromised. Attacker forged valid signatures to purchase STY at 100x discount (~687K STY for ~19.7K USDT via PancakeSwap flash loan), then dumped tokens for ~$625K USDT profit. Attack Tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0xc8c3325ba2c942a674b26de2063d278c144e92dbc91497ca0c766c915d96cbd4 Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2083039796784410802

name: Set Protocol
rootCause: The DeFi protocol Set Protocol (involving Index Coop’s ExchangeIssuance contract) was exploited due to insufficient state locking in the smart contract. The attacker used a malicious manager pre-issue hook to artificially inflate asset valuations (e.g., positionMultiplier), causing the contract to transfer excess assets based on falsified data, resulting in a loss of approximately $9,600.

name: UnprotectedArbBot
technique: Unprotected arbitrary-call forwarder drained via pre-granted WETH allowance

name: Crypto DAO
rootCause: The Pro token contract of Crypto DAO was exploited due to missing access control, with the attacker calling publicly accessible vault functions. According to GoPlus Security’s analysis, the attacker’s actual profit was approximately $52,000, while the contract lost around 167,200 Pro tokens. The related addresses monitored by Blockaid collectively held approximately $8.2 million worth of USDT (not the actual stolen amount).

name: Across
rootCause: Across Protocol attacked on Solana, ~$3.6M worth of cryptos drained. Exploiter's labeled address later refunded 331.8 ETH (~$623.9K) to Across Protocol Hub Pool Owner Multisig. Source: https://twitter.com/PeckShieldAlert/status/2082034098458214567

name: LULA
rootCause: The LULA token on BSC was exploited when attackers abused the privileged recycle() function in its contract, combined with an approximately $237 million flash loan to manipulate PancakeSwap V2 liquidity pool reserves, resulting in a loss of about $578,100.

name: WEMIX.FI Lend
rootCause: The owner privileges of a WEMIX$-related smart contract were compromised, allowing the attacker to illegally mint approximately 5.23 million WEMIX$ stablecoins (worth about $6.25 million), which were swapped into WEMIX and USDC.e before being bridged out. The team has suspended bridges and related services while working with exchanges, security firms, and law enforcement to track the funds.

name: ChainConnect
rootCause: ChainConnect bridge exploited on July 26. Attacker held ~329 ETH for ransom; whitehat agreement reached: attacker returned 280 ETH (85% of total stolen) to 0x840B3De19e3FAB72fa9A168bD8Dd71B678c57989 and retained ~49 ETH (15%) as bounty. Recovery confirmed July 31, 2026. Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0xa6df21e27c5228af87e35122b506751c642fe012b2f61c84e046625718d0c85b Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2083213179333534148

name: Garden
rootCause: Security firm Blockaid detected an ongoing exploit targeting Garden Finance’s HTLC contracts, draining about $450,000 in USDT across Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and BNB Chain. The project stated that an independent solver’s off-chain database was compromised and fraudulent records were inserted, causing improper fund releases; the protocol and smart contracts themselves were not compromised, and the app has been temporarily taken offline.

name: Projekt
rootCause: A permissionless 'buy-to-earn' reward vault (0x574f...42cb) was exploited via a flash loan attack. The attacker flash-loaned ~14K WETH from Morpho, used it to manipulate token balances across multiple Uniswap V2 memecoin pairs (Kirby Inu, ROTTSCHILD, etc.), and registered huge fake 'purchase' allocations via the unverified trackPurchase() function. The function read the buyer's token balance delta without verifying actual ETH was spent, allowing the attacker to drain ~301.7 ETH (~$560K) from the vault's reward pool via massWithdraw(). The flash loan was repaid in the same transaction. Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x90f40d3c3b60370f7287d51d972ef54596c46e98f21af91b03a4e84c5e410f64 Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2081781283584106959

name: Bankr
rootCause: The Bankrbot X account (despite on-device passkey) was compromised and posted fake airdrop links; concurrently, the project's Bankr wallet (without MFA) was drained of ~1.5 billion $BNKR tokens which were then dumped.

name: Triple-A
rootCause: Hot wallets compromised and drained across five chains (Tron 71%, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon, Solana) via automated sweep lasting ~22 hours starting July 24 at 19:31 UTC. At least $9.7M traced. Source: https://twitter.com/Phalcon_xyz/status/2082025998774657089

name: Solido Cash
rootCause: Solido Cash (the largest DeFi protocol on Supra) was exploited due to an oracle misassignment on SOLID collateral (stale feed fallback to CASH oracle, severely overvaluing collateral). The attacker, in two waves (one atomic tx + one multi-wallet manual), deposited cheap collateral, minted excess CASH, and sold it on DEXs for SUPRA, netting ~293.7M SUPRA. No user funds were affected; losses primarily hit LPs (mostly the foundation) and protocol reserves. The protocol paused relevant functions and released a forensic report.

name: Lien
rootCause: GeneralizedDotc OTC pools drained via permissionless bond group registration and flawed multiset integrity in BondMakerCollateralizedEth.exchangeEquivalentBonds(); attacker-deployed contract minted unbacked bonds with crafted payoff functions, repeated exception bondIDs to mask missing inputs, swapped worthless bonds for USDC via three pre-authorized liquidity pools; _calcRateBondToErc20 oracle inflated bond valuations. Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0xb96d572b557a12f5ef193e88cca86123a6ae1b6e98b0eeee265870c85848e0e7 Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2080531008365920472

name: AFX Bridge
rootCause: 5 of 7 bridge validator keys compromised, carrying 7,142/10,000 total power (exceeds 2/3 quorum). Two-phase attack: (1) Propose transaction with 5 compromised validator signatures, (2) Execute after 200-second dispute window to release 24.15M USDC via CCTP bridge to Ethereum. Stolen funds converted to 12,467.43 ETH at 0x627654B2782bfC57580ecD11d40869b350B6ebAC. Attack Tx: https://arbiscan.io/tx/0x50d0b3ec6c3f5fce0f10abf81540bbb508f421494aa2b3480c4a264b0436547b Source: https://twitter.com/1nf0s3cpt/status/2080082521778467217

name: AFX Trade
rootCause: Five compromised validator signatures cleared the two-thirds threshold guarding a bridge, draining $24.15 million from AFX Trade's USDC custody bridge contract on Arbitrum and moving it out through the same public rails everyone else uses.

name: VerusCoin
rootCause: A second exploit drained VerusCoin's Ethereum Bridge for $7.54 million, following a similar $11.6 million hack in May - same bridge, a different gap in the same broken trust boundary. This time there was no statement, no bounty, just silence.

name: Verus-Ethereum Bridge
rootCause: The Verus Ethereum Bridge was exploited again. The attacker abused the bridge’s import path to trigger unbacked payouts on the Ethereum side, draining approximately $7.54 million in assets (ETH, tBTC, USDC, etc.) from the bridge reserves. This is the second exploit of the same flaw from May. The project has not issued a detailed official statement yet.

name: Zilliqa
rootCause: Zilliqa announced that ZIL was stolen from a cold wallet of one of its exchange partners. Investigation confirmed the root cause was a nonce-generation vulnerability in the Zilliqa Ledger app (present since 2019), allowing private key recovery from on-chain Schnorr signatures (after ~5+ native transactions). It was not due to the exchange’s operations. Native transactions were suspended and a fix is being coordinated.

name: BSquaredNetwork
rootCause: Draining of 8.591M B2 tokens. Team estimated USD loss at approximately $3.86M USD (based on ransom demand: 10% of stolen funds = ~$386K USD). Attacker swapped stolen tokens to 1,128 ETH via WBNB intermediate and bridged out via NEAR Intents. Token price declined -15%. Attack Tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0x29d3031a1d331cffdb1607153be9ee20adcad8c55d51bc32fc96c6f358cf5ea2 Source: https://twitter.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2080060105433682085

name: Wanchain
rootCause: Wanchain’s Cardano-to-BNB Chain cross-chain bridge was exploited. The attacker drained approximately 515 million NIGHT tokens from the Cardano-side lock address. The incident may involve signature validation or replay flaws. Wanchain suspended the bridge; Midnight’s core network was unaffected. Multiple exchanges froze related funds, and NIGHT price dropped sharply before partial recovery.

name: 42DAO

name: FlyCow

The FCOW token's transfer logic allowed unauthorized burns and an immediate sync of the PancakeSwap FCOW/USDT pair during transferFrom() into the pair. This broke the DEX router's assumption that reserves would remain stable throughout the swap, enabling price distortion and draining the pool.

name: Raydium AMM
rootCause: The legacy Raydium AMM V3 program deployed on Solana lacked proper validation of the LP (liquidity provider) mint address during the liquidity withdrawal function. Because the deprecated program failed to verify that the caller-supplied LP mint matched the pool's actual registered LP mint, an attacker was able to craft a fraudulent LP mint and pass it to the withdrawal instruction, bypassing the proportion checks that govern how much liquidity can be removed. Five pools that had been deprecated since the Serum sunset in 2021 (Sollet USDT-RAY, Sollet ETH-RAY, SRM-RAY, USDC-RAY, and RAY-SOL) were drained of approximately 150,177 RAY, 5,603 SOL, and 893,700 USDC. The contracts were unreachable through Raydium's front-end but remained fully callable on-chain. Stolen assets were subsequently bridged to Ethereum and routed through Tornado Cash. Raydium's current programs use a virtual supply mechanism and enforce LP mint verification, preventing this class of attack. name: TOP Token
rootCause: The TOP Token governance system was built on Aragon DAO with a critically tiny total supply of only 16,384 TOP tokens, making it trivially inexpensive to seize majority control. The attacker acquired 8,192.000001 TOP — just over 50% of the total supply — and used this supermajority to pass a governance proposal that minted a large additional supply of TOP tokens directly to themselves. The newly minted tokens were then swapped through the TOP/WETH Balancer V1 BPool, draining 944.2 WETH (~$1.585M). The entire attack was executed in a single transaction via a dedicated exploit contract (0x25c6….729A21). Balancer V1 itself had no vulnerability; the pool was merely the exit venue where the attacker exchanged the minted tokens for liquid assets. This was a design-level failure: the governance mechanism placed no minimum token supply floor, no timelock, and no anti-dilution safeguard on minting proposals. Attack Tx: 0x967aa34c69b7775c718545c7f94d92e965eb5fc553c0f27f6f1a9c65c93ac156 Analysis: Phalcon on X

name: Flooring Protocol
rootCause: Flooring Protocol's NFT liquidity platform used a BT404-style hybrid token standard that blends fungible and non-fungible mechanics in a single contract. An integer overflow in the platform's token balance accounting logic enabled a "ghost ownership" attack: a malicious token ID could be used to satisfy one ownership check while simultaneously producing a different result in a second accounting path within the same transaction, allowing the attacker to artificially inflate their fpToken (the fungible claim token) balance to near-infinite levels. The attacker redeemed these inflated fpTokens against Flooring's NFT pools to claim underlying assets. Yuga Labs executed a white-hat intervention, pulling 68 NFTs (29 BAYC, 4 MAYC, 2 CryptoPunks, and others) worth ~$500K out of harm's way before the attacker could reach them; net losses were approximately $900K. The same vulnerable BT404/DN404 codebase was replicated in the Asterix fork, which was subsequently exploited for an additional ~$40K shortly afterward. name: Alephium Bridge
rootCause: The Alephium TokenBridge, a private fork of the Wormhole protocol using only four guardians (requiring a quorum of three signatures), contained an off-chain vulnerability in the backend software layer that processes on-chain events before submitting them to guardian signers for approval. Nearly three hours before the drain, the attacker deployed a fake-event contract on-chain whose sole purpose was to emit fabricated LOG7 events containing forged Verified Action Approval (VAA) payloads. The attacker then disrupted bridge node connectivity, forcing the backend onto a fallback validation path where events from this fake contract were ingested and forwarded to legitimate guardians. The guardians, having no way to distinguish fraudulent events from real ones at the signing layer, provided valid signatures on the forged VAAs. These signed VAAs were submitted on-chain, unlocking 200,967 USDT, 17,594 USDC, 5.18 WETH, and 0.335 WBTC on Ethereum, plus additional USDT and WBNB on BNB Chain, while simultaneously minting 13.76M unbacked wrapped ALPH tokens. Bridge guardians subsequently burned 96.4% of the unbacked wALPH through a governance recovery procedure. This was not a smart contract bug or a guardian key compromise — the flaw resided entirely in the off-chain event-processing layer. Attack Tx: 0x04128aee33a43ad4062720908c114a1416885abc9ece31eab9cc56beac4bb38b

rootCause: The ZetaChain GatewayEVM cross-chain bridge exploit chained three compounding design flaws. The attacker combined all three weaknesses across nine cross-chain transactions to drain $334K in USDC and USDT from three internal team-controlled wallets. Critically, a prior bug bounty submission that described this exact attack surface had been dismissed as 'intended behavior' by the ZetaChain team. The attacker exploited this open function to route a forged call through the EIP-7702-delegated admin EOA, causing it to satisfy the QNT pool's _isAdmin(msg.sender) check inside forwardTransaction(). This authorized a transfer of 1,988.5 QNT (~$125K) directly to the attacker's address. SlowMist detected the exploit and traced the root cause to the missing access control on the batch execution pathway. The exploit was a copycat of the Veil Cash attack disclosed days earlier; a coordinated white-hat effort subsequently recovered ~$1.84M (81%) of the stolen funds. name: Blend Pools V2
rootCause: Blend Pools V2 (specifically the YieldBlox DAO-managed lending pool on Stellar) was exploited. The attacker manipulated the price of the low-liquidity asset USTRY ~100x higher in a single trade on Stellar DEX (SDEX). This manipulated the Reflector oracle price feed. The attacker then deposited the overvalued USTRY as collateral into the Blend Pools V2 lending pool and borrowed approximately $10.2M–$10.97M worth of XLM and USDC. Stellar validators and Blockaid responded quickly, freezing a large portion (~48M XLM / ~$7.3M) of the funds. Most of the stolen assets were contained, though some USDC was bridged out.

name: IoTeX
rootCause: The IoTeX ioTube cross-chain bridge on Ethereum was drained of approximately $4.4M after an attacker compromised the private key of the account owning the bridge's Validator contract. Using the stolen key, the attacker executed a malicious contract upgrade that bypassed signature validation checks and assumed control over both the TokenSafe and MintPool contracts. The attacker then minted 410 million CIOTX tokens and drained reserve holdings of USDC, USDT, WBTC, and WETH. All stolen assets were swapped to ETH via Uniswap and bridged to Bitcoin via THORChain before any freeze could be applied. IoTeX's co-founder described it as a sophisticated, long-planned attack — with preparation spanning 6 to 18 months — consistent with insider access or advanced social engineering against key custodians. The bridge's reliance on a single validator owner key created a critical single point of failure that the attacker fully exploited. Attack Tx: 0x1b5772b2a0e1f71327e227ed4ff3ef9fbdc63a47cc8a7fb8995aab41dc7d7c3d Analysis: Halborn — Explained: The IoTeX Hack (February 2026)

name: Veil Cash
rootCause: Veil.Cash (a zk-SNARK privacy protocol on Base, forked from Tornado Cash) suffered an exploit on its legacy fixed-denomination privacy pools. Due to a misconfigured Groth16 zk-SNARK verifier (where delta2 equaled gamma2), an attacker was able to forge valid zero-knowledge proofs and drain approximately 2.9 ETH (~$5,000) in a single transaction by making multiple fraudulent withdrawals without corresponding deposits. Whitehat interveners and the exploiter voluntarily returned the funds, resulting in 100% recovery. The project’s newer/live pools were unaffected.

name: Velar Perps
rootCause: Velar Perps on Mezo lost about $401,000 on February 19, 2026 when an attacker manipulated a predictable oracle update mechanism. The exploit involved cycling trades across hundreds of wallets to repeatedly trigger manipulated price updates, draining the BTC/MUSD perpetual pool. Detection and response were delayed, and funds were ultimately bridged off Mezo and washed. The Redstone oracle used by Velar Perps updated prices in response to contract activity, lacking timestamp validation and manipulation resistance. This allowed the attacker to cycle trades and dictate oracle updates, gradually draining pool liquidity.

name: SOF Token
rootCause: The SOF token on BNB Smart Chain was exploited for approximately $225K due to a business logic flaw in its custom _update() function. During sell operations, the contract incorrectly transferred tokens directly from the Uniswap V2-compatible (PancakeSwap) liquidity pair to a burn address and immediately called sync() to update pool reserves. This sequence artificially deflated the pool's token balance without a corresponding USDT reduction, inflating the apparent SOF price within the same transaction. An attacker crafted a swap transaction that triggered this erroneous sell-side burn logic, causing the pool to burn its own liquidity and update reserves in a way that allowed the attacker to extract the pool's USDT holdings at the manipulated price. This attack pattern — abusing fee-on-transfer or burn mechanics that directly manipulate AMM balances via sync() — was a recurring vulnerability among deflationary BEP-20 tokens on BSC during early 2026. Attack Tx: 0xcb5b22d86819b84ef176aee2d6b89f687e74d829560de1bcc63d53fcb2ac68f8 Analysis: Phalcon Alert — SOF Token BSC Exploit

name: Gyro.finance
rootCause: The Gyroscope GYD L1 CCIP Escrow contract on Ethereum was exploited for approximately $700K due to an arbitrary call vulnerability in the _ccipReceive() handler. The function executed an incoming cross-chain message's recipient and data fields via a low-level functionCall() with no validation on the target address or calldata contents. An attacker sent a CCIP message from Arbitrum carrying only 1 wei of GYD, but with the recipient field set to the GYD token contract address and data encoding an approve(attacker, 2^256-1) call. Because the escrow blindly forwarded this call to the GYD token contract in its own context, the attacker obtained an unlimited token allowance over the escrow's entire GYD balance (~6.1 million GYD). A second transaction then called GYD.transferFrom(escrow, attacker, totalBalance) to drain all funds. Restricting the recipient field to exclude the GYD token contract itself would have prevented the exploit. Attack Tx: 0x51c22898a9b9f519a10b0a0be89b9d51c0248adb80cc0f89e57437e15e6c60c7 Analysis: DARKNAVY — Gyro Finance CCIP Escrow Exploit

name: Revert Lend

The attacker used a flash loan from Morpho to mint an Aerodrome concentrated liquidity NFT, deposited it as collateral, borrowed USDC, and then exploited a missing safety check in the GaugeManager contract. This allowed unstaking and withdrawing all liquidity from the debt-backed position, leaving the vault with a worthless NFT shell. A second attacker replicated it shortly after. User funds were safe; losses were mostly from Revert’s own seeded USDC. The team disabled deposits and published a post-mortem.

name: Holdstation
rootCause: The Holdstation DeFAI smart wallet platform on Berachain (chain ID 80094) suffered a $100K loss in a supply chain attack that BlockSec classified under compromised private key. An attacker stole a developer's session token, used it to bypass two-factor authentication, and injected malicious code into an application update. This gave the attacker unauthorized access to user wallet credentials through Holdstation's account abstraction infrastructure, enabling direct draining of user funds. The attack vector — credential theft leading to code injection in an update pipeline — mirrors patterns seen in broader software supply chain compromises and highlights that private key-equivalent access can be obtained through developer tooling rather than cryptographic attacks. Holdstation suspended services immediately after detection and pledged full compensation to affected users. Attack Tx: 0x63194cfda1daddb8c4e9b838f4a3736ebd7222a650fdff156bc77c2739bb2f7b Analysis: Phalcon — Holdstation Security Alert

name: SwapNet
rootCause: The SwapNet DEX aggregator router lost $13.41M across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, and BNB Smart Chain due to an arbitrary call vulnerability in its closed-source swap routing function (selector 0x87395540). For certain DEX type codes embedded in msg.data, the router performed a low-level call to a user-supplied address with user-supplied calldata and performed no validation on the call target. An attacker exploited this by specifying the USDC token contract as the target address and encoding a transferFrom(SwapNetRouter, attacker, amount) payload as calldata. Because the SwapNet router held broad (unlimited) ERC-20 approvals from users, the transferFrom call succeeded and drained all approved USDC. Twenty users were affected across four chains, with one victim losing approximately $13.34M. The vulnerability remained undetected prior to the attack because both SwapNet and its sister protocol Aperture Finance (which fell the same day for $3.67M in a related attack) were closed-source, preventing public scrutiny. Attack Tx: 0x25c08b3882ade18cbbda81521afff7239c0e91d050f6c178968802cb1b2e2b04 Analysis: BlockSec — $17M Closed-Source Smart Contract Exploit: SwapNet and Aperture Finance

name: Aperture LM
rootCause: Aperture Finance, a Uniswap V3/V4 liquidity management protocol, lost $3.67M on January 25, 2026 in the same coordinated attack wave as SwapNet. The vulnerable function (0x67b34120) executed a low-level call using a user-supplied tuple of (target, calldata, expectedOutput) without enforcing any constraints on the call target address or function selector. An attacker supplied a token contract as the target and encoded transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount) as the calldata, causing the victim contract to transfer tokens out of itself using prior ERC-20 approvals granted by users. The expectedOutput balance-delta check that was meant to validate swap results was rendered meaningless because the attacker controlled both the call and the expected result. Stolen funds, totalling approximately 1,242 ETH, were subsequently laundered through Tornado Cash. On-chain forensics linked the attacker to the same entity responsible for previous Li.Fi and Jumper Exchange exploits. Attack Tx: 0xa6fabda0bab72c210b176844e42a02c15056bca9422c6ac602e272ce1e00f689 Analysis: SolidityScan — Aperture Finance Hack Analysis

The rogue extension contained a bundled JavaScript file (4482.js) that, upon wallet unlock, captured the user's mnemonic phrase or private key via the GET_SEED_PHRASE call and silently exfiltrated it to an attacker-controlled server at api.metrics-trustwallet[.]com. Approximately $8.5 million was drained from 2,520 wallet addresses in Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana before Trust Wallet pulled the extension and replaced it with a clean v2.69. name: Ribbon
rootCause: Six days before the exploit, Ribbon Finance (operating as Aevo) deployed an oracle infrastructure update to its legacy DeFi Options Vaults (DOVs) on Ethereum. The update introduced two critical flaws: first, the oracle proxy permitted any address — not just authorized parties — to set expiry prices for newly created option series, effectively removing access control on a price-writing function; second, the update standardized oracle precision to 18 decimal places for newer tokens while older supported assets still used 8 decimal places, creating an exploitable arithmetic mismatch. The attacker created multiple minimal-collateral accounts, minted a large number of oTokens against them, then called the permissionless expiry-price setter to inject arbitrary prices at a shared expiration timestamp. With no maximum payout caps enforced per account or per option series, the attacker drained approximately $2.7 million from the legacy DOV vaults. Aevo subsequently proposed repaying active users with a 19% haircut using funds from dormant accounts. name: Panoptic V1.1
rootCause: A Cantina security researcher disclosed a critical vulnerability on August 25, 2025 in Panoptic's position fingerprint calculation algorithm. The protocol's position fingerprinting had unknowingly implemented a variant of XHASH — a cryptographic construction previously identified as insecure in academic literature — that relied on XOR operations in a manner that reduced hash collision resistance to polynomial time. This flaw allowed an attacker to spoof position ownership by crafting colliding TokenId hashes, enabling unauthorized claims over positions they did not hold and threatening approximately $5M in user funds. Weaknesses in position list validation and sanity checks that could have hinted at the issue were surfaced in Panoptic's April 2024 Code4rena audit but neither report fully described the exploit path. Upon disclosure, Panoptic coordinated a white-hat rescue operation with Cantina and Seal911, proactively securing approximately $400K in at-risk funds before any malicious actor could exploit the gap; no user funds were ultimately lost, and the disclosing researcher received a $250K bounty. The root cause was a failure to validate the source address when receiving Wormhole bridge messages: the SmartBridge's relayer registration logic did not check whether the originating address on the source chain was actually authorized. This allowed an attacker to craft a malicious bridge message on one chain (e.g., Base) that caused the SmartBridge on Ethereum or BSC to register a withdrawal without a corresponding deposit on the source chain. By exploiting this missing input validation and absent access control on Wormhole message processing, the attacker withdrew FEG tokens from the bridge contract across Ethereum, BSC, and Base without ever depositing them — draining approximately $1.3 million before selling the tokens, which caused FEG's price to collapse by 99%.
